newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom to sell $1.5 bln in snr debt - CFO.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom to sell $1.5 bln in snr debt - CFO.

text.p: WorldCom Inc plans to sell $1.5 billion of senior notes next week, according to Scott Sullivan, the company's chief financial officer.
The offering will consist of senior notes with maturities "between seven and 10-years" and will be underwritten by lead-manager Salomon Brothers Inc, Sullivan said.
"There are very attractive 10-year rates out in the marketplace and we felt it was a good time for us to have more long-term debt and to pay down bank facilities," Sullivan said.
In a written statement, WorldCom stated the proceeds from the offering will be used primarily for the repayment of bank debt, general corporate purposes and to fund expansion.

Sullivan noted about $3.4 billion of the company's roughly $4.7 billion in total outstanding debt consists of commerical bank loans. By paying down existing bank debt, he said the company would be able to "keep availability of our bank facilites so that we have a significant amount of liquidity."
The offering, which will be the first since the company's acquisition of MFS Communications Inc last year, will be a partial drawdown from a $3 billion shelf registration filed in February 12, 1997.
Sullivan said the offering will be pre-marketed this week. A roadshow will be held next Monday and Tuesday, he said.

Earlier this month, Moody's assigned a (P)Ba1 rating to the company's senior debt from its shelf offering. Standard & Poor's assigned a preliminary triple-B-minus rating to the company's senior unsecured debt from its shelf registration.
WorldCom, based in Jackson, Miss., provides local, long distance, international and Internet services primarily to primarily business customers.
